en: To regard something as caused by; a quality or feature
hook: ATTRIBUTE: give TRIBUTE (credit) to the cause.
story: Nadia attributed her success to her mother's sacrifices and her own daily discipline. Patience is her best attribute. To attribute is to credit to a cause; as a noun, an attribute is a quality. Synonyms: ascribe, impute.

en: Causing great disaster or misfortune
hook: CALAMITOUS: a CALAMITY.
story: The bridge collapse was calamitous: dozens dead, the region cut off for months, and businesses ruined. Calamitous means disastrous. Synonyms: catastrophic, cataclysmic, ruinous.

en: To examine and remove objectionable parts from media
hook: CENSOR: CUTS out what's forbidden. Not censure (criticize).
story: The government censored the film, cutting every scene that criticized the police. The journalist's article was censored too. To censor is to suppress or remove content. Don't confuse it with censure, which means to criticize formally.

en: To publicly support or fight for a cause
hook: GRE trick: to CHAMPION a cause means to fight FOR it.
story: For forty years, the lawyer championed the rights of garment workers, fighting for safer factories and fair wages. To champion means to vigorously support a cause. Synonyms: advocate, espouse, defend.

en: To make a problem worse
hook: GRE trick: COMPOUND interest grows; a COMPOUNDED problem grows worse.
story: Rafi missed the bus, and then compounded his problem by taking a wrong shortcut that led him even further away. To compound means to make worse, adding problem on problem. Synonyms: exacerbate, aggravate.

en: To discourage someone from doing something, usually by fear
hook: DETER: like a TERROR that keeps you away.
story: The security cameras and bright lights deterred thieves from targeting the shop. Heavy fines deter people from littering. To deter is to discourage, usually through fear of consequences. A deterrent is something that deters.

en: Skillful, especially with the hands
hook: DEXTEROUS: DEXTER is Latin for right hand, the skilled hand.
story: The dexterous tailor threaded a needle in one second and stitched a perfect buttonhole without looking. Dexterous means skillful with the hands. Synonyms: deft, adroit, nimble.

en: A formal or authoritative statement; a short saying
hook: DICTUM: what is DICTATED, spoken (dictus).
story: The old teacher's dictum, 'Read every day, even one page,' stayed with Tanvir for life. A dictum is an authoritative statement or maxim. Synonyms: pronouncement, maxim, aphorism.

en: Conscientiously fulfilling one's duties
hook: DUTIFUL: full of DUTY.
story: Every evening, the dutiful daughter rushed home after work to cook for her ailing father and give him his medicine. Dutiful means faithfully performing duties. Synonyms: conscientious, obedient.

en: Able to understand and share the feelings of others
hook: EMPATHETIC: feeling IN (em) someone else's pain (pathos).
story: The empathetic doctor sat with the frightened patient, held her hand, and said, 'I understand. I'd be scared too.' Empathetic means understanding and sharing another's feelings. Empathy is deeper than sympathy.

en: To happen afterward as a result
hook: ENSUE: follows like a SEQUEL.
story: The referee made a bad call, and chaos ensued: players shouted, fans threw bottles, and the match was stopped. To ensue is to follow as a result. Synonyms: follow, result.

en: To understand after much thought
hook: FATHOM: measuring deep water — and deep ideas.
story: Mitu couldn't fathom why her friend had suddenly stopped speaking to her; she replayed every conversation but found nothing. To fathom is to understand deeply. A fathom is also a unit of water depth.

en: Open, honest, and direct
hook: FRANK: Frank always tells it straight.
story: 'To be frank,' said the professor, 'your proposal needs a lot of work.' Arif appreciated the honesty. Frank means open and direct. Synonyms: candid, blunt, forthright.

en: Relevant to the subject
hook: GERMANE: GERMAN relatives belong to the family — relevant.
story: In the debate, the judge stopped Rafi: 'Your point about football isn't germane to the topic of climate policy.' Germane means relevant. Synonyms: pertinent, apposite, apropos.

en: To complain in a bad-tempered, muttering way
hook: GRUMBLE: like a grumbling, rumbling stomach.
story: The passengers grumbled about the delay, muttering and checking their watches, but nobody actually complained to the staff. To grumble is to complain in a low, irritable voice. Synonyms: mutter, gripe.

en: Unwilling to accept new ideas; narrow and conventional
hook: HIDEBOUND: bound tight in an old HIDE (skin).
story: The hidebound committee rejected online classes: 'We've always taught in classrooms, and we always will.' Hidebound means rigidly conventional. Synonyms: conservative, narrow-minded, ossified.

en: A person who claims beliefs or virtues they don't follow
hook: HYPOCRITE: a Greek actor (hypokrites), playing a role.
story: The politician lectured citizens about saving electricity while his own mansion's air conditioners ran day and night. People called him a hypocrite. A hypocrite pretends to have virtues they lack.

en: Unwise; likely to cause trouble or offense
hook: IM-POLITIC: NOT POLITIC, not diplomatic.
story: Criticizing your boss in the company group chat is impolitic, even if you're right. Tanvir learned this the hard way. Impolitic means unwise and tactless. Synonyms: imprudent, injudicious.

en: Proceeding gradually and subtly, but with harmful effects
hook: INSIDIOUS: sneaks INSIDE you quietly.
story: Diabetes can be insidious: no pain, no obvious symptoms, while silently damaging the body for years. Insidious means harmful in a gradual, hidden way. Synonyms: pernicious, stealthy, treacherous.

en: A person who acts as a link between two parties
hook: INTER-MEDIARY: in the MIDDLE between.
story: Since the two companies refused to talk directly, a retired judge acted as intermediary, carrying proposals back and forth. An intermediary is a go-between. Synonyms: mediator, middleman.

en: Accepting what happens without active response or resistance
hook: PASSIVE: lets everything PASS by without acting.
story: Rafi was passive in meetings, never sharing ideas, just nodding at whatever others decided. His manager wanted him to speak up. Passive means inactive and accepting. Its opposite is active or assertive.

en: Good-humored teasing
hook: RAILLERY: friends RALLY around you with jokes.
story: At the wedding, the groom endured hours of raillery from his friends: jokes about his dancing, his speech, and his nervous sweating. Everyone laughed, including him. Raillery is friendly teasing. Synonyms: banter, badinage.

en: To talk or write at length in a confused, aimless way; to walk aimlessly
hook: RAMBLE: like a RAMBLING road with no destination.
story: Asked a simple question, the old man rambled for twenty minutes about his school days, his cousin's wedding, and the price of fish in 1985. To ramble is to talk aimlessly. It also means to wander leisurely.

en: To feel bitterness about unfair treatment
hook: RE-SENT: the insult is SENT back again and again in your mind.
story: Mitu resented her brother for getting a new bicycle while she got nothing. Even years later, she remembered it. To resent is to feel bitter about something unfair. Resentment builds when it isn't discussed.

en: Remaining after most has gone
hook: RESIDUAL: the RESIDUE left behind.
story: Even after the flood waters receded, residual damp remained in the walls for months. Residual fear stayed with the children too. Residual means remaining or leftover. Synonyms: vestigial, lingering.

en: Firm determination; to decide firmly or settle
hook: RESOLVE: a RESOLUTION you stick to.
story: After failing once, Arif's resolve only grew stronger; he studied every day for a year and passed with distinction. As a noun, resolve means firm determination. As a verb, it means to decide, or to solve a problem.

en: A substitute, especially a person acting in another's place
hook: SURROGATE: a SUBSTITUTE who stands in.
story: When their parents worked abroad, the children's grandmother became a surrogate mother, raising them with love. A surrogate is a substitute. Surrogate mothers carry babies for other couples.

en: To speak or write about in an abusively disparaging manner
hook: VILIFY: make someone a VILLAIN.
story: The tabloids vilified the young actress for weeks, calling her selfish and dishonest over a misunderstanding. Later, the truth showed she was innocent. To vilify is to portray someone as evil. Synonyms: malign, defame, denigrate.

en: Lacking; not good enough
hook: GRE trick: FOUND WANTING means found lacking, not desiring.
story: When the cyclone came, the emergency plan was found wanting: not enough shelters, boats, or food. On the GRE, wanting means lacking or deficient, not desiring. Her essay was wanting in evidence.

en: Intentional; stubbornly determined to do as one wants
hook: WILL-FUL: full of your own WILL.
story: It wasn't an accident; it was willful damage, done on purpose. The willful child refused every instruction and did exactly as she pleased. Willful means deliberate, or stubbornly self-willed. Synonyms: headstrong, intentional.
